locations.name: Bretonnian Lands
locations.role: Broad western cultural-geographic region analogous to medieval Europe: politically fragmented into kingdoms, duchies, counties, free cities, ecclesiastical territories, marches and lordships, but linked by chivalric culture, religion, related language, customs, heraldry and social institutions.

locations.name: Kingdom of Bretonnia
locations.role: One of the largest, richest and most prestigious realms within the Bretonnian Lands, ruled by King Charles III. Its use of the name Bretonnia is itself a claim to primacy and representative leadership over the wider Bretonnian world.

locations.name: Bellacourt
locations.role: Capital of the Kingdom of Bretonnia and host of Charles III's royal court, Grand Tourney, markets, guilds and cathedral.

locations.name: Côte de Lys
locations.role: Royal palace or citadel of King Charles III in Bellacourt.

locations.name: Notre-Dame du Lys
locations.formal_name: Cathedral of Our Lady of the Sacred Lily
locations.role: Major center of Church authority in Bellacourt. Its common name deliberately evokes old Bretonnian religious tradition, while its formal dedication is to Our Lady of the Sacred Lily.
Site of the Grand Tourney, which also functions as a display of Charles III's prestige and diplomatic influence.
Undecided location where the Holy Relic is recovered.

locations.name: Bellacourt
locations.role: Bellacourt, including Côte de Lys and the city's defenses, is the currently preferred setting for the climactic siege. The exact military geography and reason Charles III and Alaric are caught there remain unresolved.

Planned final reward: a modest lordship or estate roughly abbey-sized, centered on a small fort or Dragon Rider chapter house, with limited vassals and practical feudal rights such as fishing, hunting, and possibly a small mine or other local resource. Exact location, title, boundaries and obligations remain TODOs.
